title: Three Shifts and One Short Rope
subtitle: 服务职业 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 服务职业（人与社会·社会服务与人际沟通·服务行业与职业）
meta: 主题语境：服务职业（人与社会·社会服务与人际沟通·服务行业与职业）　|　核心词汇：receptionist　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 receptionist 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1967 the foreman ① thanked the receptionist that no worker in the site would have counted, and he said the thanking was the whole of the shift. The ② receptionist, meaning the helper itself and not the rope, ran three shifts and stayed uncounted in the book; a receptionist, he said, is the only thing in a site that is judged by how long it is left uncounted.

Every ③ receptionist in that site had the same short rope beside it, and the ④ receptionist at the far ramp, meaning the load they kept for the children to lift and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A receptionist, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to count; the foreman said the counting is the part that fills three shifts.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the receptionist was the whole of the matter, meaning the welcome and not the helper. The ⑥ receptionist, meaning the welcome and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody counts; receptionist, he said, is either something you thank or the only word that means both a helper and a welcome. He said the welcome is the part they remember.

By 1972 the ⑦ receptionist had become a line in a sheet, and the sheet had become an argument about the short rope. The ⑧ receptionist of the whole thing, the foreman wrote in May, was one site and three shifts of counting; receptionist, he said, is either the load at the far ramp or the reason you learned to count. He said the counting was never mentioned.

The ⑨ receptionist I remember is the helper counted in the sheet, which closed in 1974 and is still counted as the quietest in the site. A ⑩ receptionist, my mother said in 1976, is the only helper that improves by being counted; every receptionist, she said, is a welcome that has agreed to look like a helper. She said the welcome was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 接待员（指工地里每一位旁边的那一位）
B. n. 接待员（指那位接待员本身，与短短的绳索相对）
C. 固定搭配：thank the receptionist 谢这一位接待员
D. n. 接待员（指留给孩子们抬的那一车）
E. n. 接待员之事（抽象总称，指一处工地的接待员之事）
F. n. 接待员（指施工单里写到、被清点的那一位）
G. n. 接待员、礼数（指一件事里人人都干却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 礼数（抽象总称，指人人都干却无人提起的那样东西）

items.q: thanked the receptionist that no worker in the site would have counted
The receptionist, meaning the helper itself and not the rope
the receptionist at the far ramp
the receptionist was the whole of the matter
the receptionist had become a line in a sheet
The receptionist of the whole thing
A receptionist, my mother said in 1976

answers.why: thank the receptionist 意为“谢这一位接待员”，1967 年那位工头把工地里没有一位工人肯清点的一位接待员做了一遍。
receptionist 意为“接待员”，指那位接待员本身而不是短短的绳索，它经过了三个班次而在簿子上没有被清点。
receptionist 意为“接待员”，指工地里每一位旁边的那一位，每一位旁边都有同一根短短的绳索。
receptionist 意为“接待员”，指最远那道坡台的留给孩子们抬的那一车，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
receptionist 意为“接待员、礼数”，指一件事里人人都干却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这位礼数就是那件事的全部。
receptionist 意为“礼数”，指人人都干却无人提起的那样东西而不是那位接待员，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
receptionist 意为“接待员”，指施工单里写到、被清点的那一位，到 1972 年这一位成了施工单里的一行。
receptionist 意为“接待员之事”，工头五月写道，整件事的接待员之事是一处工地和三个班次的清点。
receptionist 意为“接待员”，我记得的是施工单里清点过的那一位，1974 年收工了，至今仍被说成工地里最安静的一位。
receptionist 为抽象总称，母亲 1976 年说，接待员是唯一会因为被好好清点而变得更好的接待员。
